correctness.rationale: The box contains the polytope and its two antipodal corners force the unique minimum enclosing sphere, with binary nonconstant corners excluded by a forbidden full-to-zero cyclic transition. For a nonouter vertex some difference facet x_i-x_{i+1}=a_i-ell is tight. Setting t=x_{i+1} in [0,ell], its two radial-deficit terms give the strictly concave quadratic f(t)=(a_i-ell+t)(ell-t)+t(a_{i+1}-t), minimized at t=0 or ell; both endpoint values are >=ell(b-ell). Equality requires a single nonbox coordinate at a minimum-length chain, all others box endpoints and one cyclic backward full block. Active-coordinate constraints plus a tight difference facet prove each listed configuration is a vertex. The separate endpoint patterns have 2(s-1) members per minimum index when b>2ell and merge into s at b=2ell. This logic covers s=2 and arbitrary admissible real parameters. A second rational active-facet intersection implementation rechecked all 56 binary-length profiles for s=2,3,4 with ell=1,2; these finite checks merely corroborate the all-real proof.

value.rationale: The first strict interior vertex-radius level is a natural metric invariant of the full, Euclidean-embedded chainlink polytope and measures robustness of its two-point circumsphere contact set. The sharp gap and entire equality stratum, especially the collapse at a_i=2ell, are useful beyond the known total vertex enumeration. The geometry is not a disguised citation of the total vertex count; the equality-phase transition and use of the minimum link length require a separate extremal argument.

final_claim: For all s>=2, ell>0 and real a_i>=2ell, the unique minimal enclosing sphere of CL(a,ell) is centered at a/2 and meets only 0 and a. The minimum positive squared-radius deficit among vertices is ell(min_i a_i-ell), attained at exactly 2m(s-1) vertices when min a_i>2ell, or ms at equality, where m is the number of minimum components.
